views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold a firm negotiating posture and keep the talks channel open rather than escalating further. We have already retaliated on the ~$60B US-goods list (May 13) and now face 25% tariffs across ~$250B of our exports with an additional ~$300B tranche threatened; escalating again would only invite that tranche and deepen damage to an already-slowing economy. We should signal readiness to resume high-level talks on terms that defend our core red lines (no capitulation on Huawei or structural tech concessions) while avoiding actions that hand Washington a pretext to widen the war.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is high. On 2019-05-15 the US put Huawei on the Entity List (EO 13873) — direct firm-level targeting of our flagship technology champion and a frontal challenge to our tech self-sufficiency agenda; the same week, List 3 tariffs were raised from 10% to 25% (2019-05-10, on top of the ~$50B already at 25%) and Trump ordered preparation of tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of our exports (2019-05-05). This sits at the high anchor for CHN: major export sectors hit, firm-level targeting of Huawei, and FX/growth pressure. Critically, the macro confirms the bite: April industrial output grew only 5.4% y/y, far below the 6.5% expected and down sharply from March's 8.5%, with retail sales faltering (Reuters/NBS, 2019-05-15) — evidence that the trade war is eroding growth just as we face an even tougher tariff regime. The action stance is deliberately moderate: given this weakening macro base and the imminent ~$300B escalation threat, escalating further would be self-destructive, while full concession would be politically untenable domestically after the Huawei attack. Negotiating from a firm base — leveraging the fact the US also faces market stress (US 10y yield fell to 2.37%, VIX elevated — signaling the tariff escalation is hurting US markets too) — is the sound route to ease the spiral without capitulating.
key_factors: Huawei Entity List / EO 13873 (2019-05-15) — direct hit on flagship tech firm and tech self-sufficiency agenda
List 3 tariffs lifted 10%→25% (2019-05-10); ~$250B of Chinese exports now at 25%
US threatened additional ~$300B tranche on remaining Chinese imports (2019-05-05)
China already retaliated May 13 on its ~$60B US-goods list
April industrial output +5.4% y/y (vs 6.5% expected, down from 8.5% in March) — economy already weakening
US market stress (10y at 2.37%, elevated VIX) gives negotiating leverage
